text:
Ari: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands about runtime ops. Two things we need clarified: the 'latency-first' behavior of adaptive microbatching, and the recommended canary prewarm strategy for KV/prefix caches.

Neha: Good callout. Adaptive microbatching exposes `max_batch_wait_ms` and `preferred_latency_target_ms` per route. If you set latency-first, the runtime lowers batch windows proactively and opts into the fast-path kernel for short sequences.

Ravi: Is `preferred_latency_target_ms` part of the route manifest or the model bundle? Need to put defaults in infra templates.

Neha: It's a route manifest field. We'll add sane defaults in the infra repo (PLG/Mid/Enterprise presets). Example: `preferred_latency_target_ms: 30` for PLG, `15` for Enterprise.

Sofia: On canaries: our recommended plan is prewarm + slow ramp. Start with 1% traffic after prewarm script, 10m steady, then 10% for 5m, then 50% if healthy. Prewarm script lives at `ops/scripts/prewarm_prefixes.sh`.

Ari: What happens if prewarm is skipped? We've seen p95 spikes and some transient errors in past canaries.

Neha: If you skip prewarm, expect cache cold-start regrowth. That can spike memory and latency as many threads populate the KV cache. For chat-heavy workloads we strongly recommend prewarm. For stateless batch workloads, prewarm adds little value and can increase memory.

Ravi: Any runtime flags to limit memory growth during prewarm?

Neha: Yes — `cache.prewarm_max_entries` and `cache.memory_budget_mb`. Also `cache.mode: prewarm` vs `cache.mode: none` for canaries so you don't mix states.

DevOps-Bot: Canary started: route redwood/v2-small -> canary-2024-04-03 (1% traffic)

Priya: From infra: we'll push template changes to `infra/templates/route.yaml` with the new fields and defaults. I'll open a PR with the sample route and prewarm job.

Sofia: Runtime note: the next runtime patch includes a lightweight fast-path kernel that avoids redundant copies for short-context requests. Microbenchmarks show ~25% p95 improvement for small prompts. Landing in v0.9.12.

Ari: Great. Can we get a tiny perf harness to run on dedicated clusters before switching traffic?

Sofia: Yes — adding a minimal `perf-checker` in `platform/tools/perf-checker`. It runs a representative prompt set at configurable QPS and outputs p50/p95/p99 + mem. Will link PR.

Neha: Also scheduling a focused office hours next Thursday for SEs on canary strategies and batching knobs. Will post calendar invite.

Ari: Thanks, all. Please drop the infra PR and the perf runner link here once ready.

Priya: Will do.
